devotions.titel: Here I Am, Whatever It Costs
devotions.citaat: But even when we couldn't control our circumstances, we could still choose how we respond to God.

zinnen.tekst: My husband ... and I pastor a church in Tel Aviv, in Israel. And if you follow the news at all, then you would know that the last few years have been challenging ... We've lived through three wars. We've spent countless nights in bomb shelters. We've had so many sleepless nights where we've been given 90 seconds to run from our beds to the bomb shelter at the end of the street. ... And I can tell you this, when you're sitting in a bomb shelter at 3 in the morning, tired, afraid and unsure of what tomorrow will bring, there is one thing that you become painfully painfully aware of, and that is that you have no control over anything. We had plans. Plans for our church, plans for our lives, things we wanted to build, things we were looking forward to, things we'd work towards, and then all of a sudden, overnight, all these plans were just turned upside down.

And suddenly we couldn't even plan what the next day would look like, much less what the future would hold. But even when we couldn't control our circumstances, we could still choose how we respond to God. And in those moments, there was one word that kept coming back to me, and that word is hineni. Hineni is a Hebrew word ... In the Bible, it isn't a word that just states a location. It is actually a powerful declaration of readiness to the Lord, to serve him with whatever you have, to surrender to him completely, no matter the cost. It says as much as I'm listening, I'm ready, I'm all yours, I'm here to serve you.

But the first person in scripture to say Hineni to God is not actually Isaiah, it is Abraham. And he said it not just once, he says it twice. ... And now God calls Abraham. And Abraham says for the first time in the Bible, Yes, God, I'm ready, I'm yours to do whatever you want me to do. He surrendered himself completely to God without knowing what lied ahead. ... But then God asked Abraham to do one of the hardest things ever imaginable, to sacrifice Isaac, the son he had waited for for so long ... But the second time Abraham knew what it would cost him. It was a yes to God, not just to uncertainty, but to hardship. And that matters for us because most of us have given our hineni to God at some point to uncertainty. We've given our yes to God to follow Him. Maybe even our yes to ministry, yes to serving, yes to the unknown. But are we ready to give a hineni to hardship as well? A hineni that remains when the cost becomes visible?

gebed.tekst: Holy Spirit, we just say, come. More. ... The Holy Spirit comes because Jesus promised you would. So Lord, just let your anointing begin to flow. More. Fill people. Fill. He's here. ... Surrender that hurt. ... Surrender that pain from the past. Surrender that bitterness. Surrender it. Surrender. ... Come. Come. Come. Come. ... Let your oil heal. ... Amen.

devotions.bijbelvers: Whom then shall I send and who will go for us? ... Here I am, send to me.

vraag.tekst: But are we ready to give a hineni to hardship as well? A hineni that remains when the cost becomes visible?

devotions.titel: Prepare, Keep Going, Surrender the Outcome
devotions.citaat: Our responsibility is just obedience. The outcome belongs to God.

zinnen.tekst: The first thing is that giving our hineni means we prepare. So Abram's hineni, his wholehearted yes to God, was actually not coming out of the blue. It was the fruit of years spent walking with God. Learning his character, trusting him, knowing his faithfulness. And when uncertainty and hardship came, Abram already knew the God he was trusting. ... But we can get to know him, not just in times of crisis, but actually before that, when times are good. ... We can develop habits of prayer, of worship, of obedience, of trust. And an important one that Abraham didn't yet have is that we can actually read and study his word, the Bible. I cannot tell you how much it helped us in times of uncertainty and difficulty when we didn't feel the presence of God to know what he was saying about us. ... Not because we felt it, but because His Word says so.

Coming back to Abraham ... when God tells him to take Isaac, he obeys. Humanly speaking, that would have been the moment to retreat. ... And that matters because in seasons of uncertainty or hardship, one of the greatest temptations is to withdraw. To stop serving, to stop believing. To wait until things calm down a little bit. ... Not having all the answers, but continuing to walk with him anyways. Continuing to trust him, continuing to obey him, continuing to walk with him. And stay faithful to him even when the season is hard. ... But as followers of Jesus, we're actually not called to be in survival mode. We're actually called to bring light into difficult seasons. To bring hope where people are losing hearts. To carry peace into confusion, truth into chaos, and peace into these places that feel overwhelmed. ... And to ask God, Lord, how can I serve you? What do you want me to do in this season?

Our surrender to God cannot depend on the outcome. Because if we're honest, we often say yes to God with certain expectations. We take a step of faith and we expect doors to open. We serve faithfully and we expect to see fruits. We pray for people and we expect them to grow. ... And of course there's nothing wrong with expecting big things from God. We should be believing Him for great things. But there's a difference between believing God for an outcome and making the outcome the condition of our obedience. Because sometimes we obey and things just don't turn out the way we want them to. We pray and the answer doesn't come. We pour into people and they still walk away. ... But Abraham's faith was actually not rooted in knowing how the story would end. It was rooted in knowing the God who had called him. ... He asks us to be faithful with what he has given to us and leave the outcome to him. Our responsibility is just obedience. The outcome belongs to God. ... It means here I am because I trust you, even if the circumstances do not make any sense.

Surrender that hurt. ... Surrender that pain from the past. Surrender that bitterness. Surrender it. Surrender. ... Come. Come. Come. Come. ... Let your oil heal. ... Amen.

devotions.titel: He Said Here I Am First
devotions.citaat: But the most beautiful thing about Hineni is that it's not actually about our commitment to God. It's about His commitment to us.

zinnen.tekst: But there's something even greater about Hineni that I actually want to end with. Something I have to remind myself over and over and over again. Because looking at these three points, it would be easy to think that getting through these seasons of uncertainty and hardship depends entirely on us. But the most beautiful thing about Hineni is that it's not actually about our commitment to God. It's about His commitment to us. ... Our yes to God is only ever a response to him, to his invitation, to his extended hand, to his absolute yes to us, fully devoted to us. Because before we ever said here I am, he said it to us. In Isaiah 58:9 God gives this promise and he says, then you will call and the Lord will answer, you will cry for help and he will say, here I am.

And I love this because God doesn't say, I will get to it when I get to it, or I will be there someday. He says, here I am, fully devoted to us. And maybe you're in this season of uncertainty or hardship right now, and God feels distant. Maybe you're carrying questions that haven't been answered yet. And this promise is for you. The God we follow is not absent in our struggle. He is so present in the midst of it. And God did not just say he did, he showed it to us. This brings us back to Abram. When Abram was about to sacrifice Isaac, God stopped him and he provided a ram in Isaac's place. It is almost as if he was saying, Abram, you don't have to give your beloved son because one day I will give mine. And the sacrifice that God spared Abraham from making, he would one day make himself on that same ridge of hills. And that is exactly what he did in Jesus.

When Adam and Eve had sin in the garden, God came looking for them. And he called for them. Where are you? ... But instead of saying, here I am, humanity's first response to God after sin entered the world was ... fear and hiding. But God didn't stop pursuing humanity. And all of heaven and earth moved towards that point where he would come and provide what only he could do and he would surrender what only he could do. Thousands of years later in another garden, the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus knowing the suffering that lay ahead, knowing the cost of the cross, would kneel there and say, not my will be done, but yours Lord, Hineni. ... We surrendered to God who entered our suffering when the cost was greatest, who remained faithful and who is still faithful today. ... And that's why we surrender ... not because we know how everything will turn out, but because we know the one we are surrendering to.

No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. ... The ultimate act of surrender that we know from the Bible is Jesus laying down his own life. And he says this phrase, of my own accord, telling us that it was voluntary, that his surrender was not coerced, it was not forced, it was not persuaded. But this means that the cross was not something done to him, but rather something done by Him. An act of surrender that was completely limited to His control. And every day we're faced with the same decision of whether we will live a life of surrender.

In Luke chapter 4, Jesus was filled with the Spirit. He was led by the Spirit into a desert. Then the Bible says He returned in the power of the Spirit. ... And when we talk about deserts, we often talk about them as a place of disconnection. ... God first spoke to Abraham in a desert. God spoke to Moses in a desert. God spoke to Isaiah in a desert and God spoke to Jesus in a desert. In fact it was in the desert they heard the voice of God. ... So when you're in a desert season you're closer to God than you think. Don't pray for deliverance from the desert. No, pray that you'll hear the voice of God in the desert. ... You can be in a desert season and have no clarity, no direction and still be full of the Holy Spirit. You see the only distance between you and the Holy Spirit is your unawareness of Him.

In his interview, he was asked this question, what is the number one vulnerability that takes most leaders out ... And he was talking about high level leaders. He was talking about CEOs, senior pastors, those at the top of the corporation. What's the number one vulnerability that they have that takes them out? ... Was it money? Was it fame? Sin? Sex? Mistakes? Failure? The number one thing ... said that takes most high level leaders out is one word, ego. See, ego is everything that works against surrender. Because my ego is filled by my flesh. And we can't be believers that are led by our flesh. We have to be led by the Spirit. You see, public authority can only rest on private surrender. You won't miss that ego. ... You won't miss that bitterness. But it starts by surrender. You see, surrender isn't about losing as it is much about loving.

devotions.titel: Not Your Reward but Your Gift
devotions.citaat: We get the Spirit at salvation. But the Spirit gets us at surrender.

zinnen.tekst: 1 Peter 1 verse 8, Peter says, Though you have not seen him, you love him because you believe in him. How do you surrender daily to someone that you don't see? Because Jesus was visible, but the Holy Spirit is invisible. ... So how do you fellowship with someone invisible? The Bible tells us in 2 Corinthians 5 verse 7, we live by faith and not by sight. Fellowshiping with the Holy Spirit is not by sight, it's by faith. It's by faith I surrender to him daily. And you say that God, it would have been so much easier if you gave the Holy Spirit a body like Jesus. Then I could fellowship with him. But God says, I did give him a body. I gave him yours. You are the temple of the Holy Spirit.

He's the great revealer of Jesus. You see, the more I surrender to the Holy Spirit, the closer I get to Jesus. The biggest thing that stops people surrendering to the Holy Spirit is we don't feel worthy. Well, you don't know what I did last year. ... You don't know what I did last week, last night. And we make the Holy Spirit reward-based and not relationship-based. But he's not your reward. He's your gift. You see, some people say, oh, you can only fellowship with the Holy Spirit when you're completely pure. But that's not true. None of us are perfect. None of us are mistake-free. No, purity is not an accomplishment. Purity is a relationship. The Holy Spirit is the one that comes in and makes us pure. The more I come into his presence, the more I lean on him. The more I fellowship with him. The more I have intimacy with him. He purifies me.

But none of us are perfect. And it's wrong to interpret holiness as perfection. That's not what holiness is. It's not perfect behavior. ... The Holy Spirit is not the reward for your holiness. The Holy Spirit is the source of your holiness. ... A young man come to me four weeks ago. We run these nights in South Africa ... And they're nights where we just let the Holy Spirit move. ... He said, I've been addicted to pornography for eight years. He said, but I came that night and I got touched by ... Holy Spirit in a way I'd never experienced before. ... And he said, I went home. And he said, I kept reading my Bible, but I started to fellowship with the Holy Spirit. And he said, after three months, I noted something. I hadn't looked at porn. He said, after six months, I had no desire for porn. ... Let me tell you something, one touch of the Holy Spirit can start personal revival in a person's heart. It's a life of surrendering to him. Oh, we repent enough to be forgiven, but can we surrender enough to be changed? ... We get the Spirit at salvation. But the Spirit gets us at surrender.

devotions.titel: Empty Yourself, Yield to His Presence
devotions.citaat: Relationship with the Holy Spirit is more important than revelation from the Holy Spirit.

zinnen.tekst: You see the Holy Spirit. He's not a power. He's a person. If the Holy Spirit was a power, it would surrender to you. But if the Holy Spirit is a person, we must surrender to him. ... He's not a something, he's a someone ... No, he is a person that desires intimacy with you. James 4 verse 5 says he desires us. ... When we see the Holy Spirit as a power, we only want to use him. But when we see the Holy Spirit as a person, we want him to use us. ... Do you remember the story of Elijah on the mountain? 1 Kings chapter 19 verse 11. The Lord said, go and stand on the mountain in the presence of the Lord. The Lord's about to pass by. The Bible says at first there was a great wind. Then there was an earthquake. Then there was a fire. ... But these are only manifestations of the Holy Spirit. That's not where he is found. Where did Elijah find him? It was not in the earthquake. It was in a still, small voice. ... But a voice can only be attributed to a person. Relationship with the Holy Spirit is more important than revelation from the Holy Spirit.

If I can leave you with anything today, it's to learn a life of surrender, to empty yourself, to yield yourself to his presence. ... You can get to the place where the empowerment of the anointing of the Holy Spirit of Jesus will come on you as soon as you surrender, as soon as you yield, and that's when his power moves. That's when his fruit flows. ... But you have to learn, and I'll close with this, you have to learn to be a vessel. ... You've got to learn to be a vessel of the Holy Spirit. A vessel of Jesus to this world. You have an assignment to your community, to your workplace, to your school, to your country, to your city. ... You see, vessels surrender to the one that holds them. Vessels are a steward of what they carry. Vessels hold his power. ... You have an anointing from the anointed one. And the more you surrender to the anointed one, the more his anointing flows.

I want to teach you how to surrender. How you surrender is you empty yourself. You empty yourself. I like to put my hands out like this with my palms facing up. And I just ask the Holy Spirit to come. And you've got to learn to yield. You've got to learn to be still. ... There's something about stillness where we're still that the Spirit begins to move. ... You don't need a song for the Holy Spirit. You don't need a service. You don't need a sound. You don't need a speaker. No, the Holy Spirit doesn't come because of those things. The Holy Spirit comes because Jesus promised you would. ... Surrender that hurt. ... Surrender that pain from the past. Surrender that bitterness. Surrender it. Surrender. ... One moment with the Holy Spirit ... It can bring peace. It can bring clarity. It can bring answers. It can bring solution. And it can bring breakthrough in the way you need Him in your life.

delen.titel: Here I Am, Whatever It Costs
delen.citaat: But are we ready to give a hineni to hardship as well? A hineni that remains when the cost becomes visible?
delen.uitleg: The first speaker pastors a church in Tel Aviv and tells of three wars, bomb shelters and plans turned upside down overnight. In the shelter at three in the morning you become painfully aware that you have no control over anything, but you can still choose how you respond to God. The word that kept coming back was hineni, here I am: a declaration of readiness to the Lord, to surrender to Him completely, no matter the cost (Isaiah 6:8). Abraham said it twice: first to complete uncertainty, and then on the way to sacrifice Isaac, when he knew what it would cost him. Most of us have given our yes to uncertainty; the question is whether we are ready to give a hineni to hardship as well.
delen.vraag: Where have you said 'here I am' to God in uncertainty, and how is it for you to say it again now that you can see what it costs?

delen.titel: Prepare, Keep Going, Surrender the Outcome
delen.citaat: But there's a difference between believing God for an outcome and making the outcome the condition of our obedience.
delen.uitleg: Three things they learned in the hard season. Prepare: Abraham's yes was the fruit of years of walking with God, so when hardship came he already knew the God he was trusting; we can get to know Him when times are good, through habits of prayer, worship, obedience and trust, and by reading and studying His Word, so that what holds us is not what we feel but what He has said. Keep going: in Genesis 22 Abraham obeys the next day, while our temptation is to withdraw and quietly pull back our yes; as followers of Jesus we are not called to survival mode but to bring light, hope and peace into difficult seasons. Surrender the outcome: there is nothing wrong with expecting big things from God, but there is a difference between believing Him for an outcome and making the outcome the condition of our obedience. Our responsibility is obedience; the outcome belongs to God.
delen.vraag: Which outcome are you still holding on to as the condition of your obedience, and what would it mean to leave it with Him?

delen.titel: He Said Here I Am First
delen.citaat: Jesus knowing the suffering that lay ahead, knowing the cost of the cross, would kneel there and say, not my will be done, but yours Lord, Hineni.
delen.uitleg: Then the speaker turns the three points over: the most beautiful thing about hineni is that it is not about our commitment to God but about His commitment to us. Our yes is only ever a response to His yes, because before we ever said here I am, He said it to us; in Isaiah 58:9 He promises that when you cry for help He will say, here I am. God did not just say it, He showed it: when Abraham was about to sacrifice Isaac, God provided a ram, as if to say, you do not have to give your beloved son, because one day I will give mine, and that is exactly what He did in Jesus. In the first garden humanity's answer to 'where are you?' was fear and hiding; in Gethsemane Jesus knelt and said, not my will but yours. We surrender to a God who entered our suffering when the cost was greatest and who is still faithful today.
delen.vraag: What changes for you when surrender starts with His 'here I am' to you, and with what Jesus gave in Gethsemane, instead of with your own commitment?

delen.citaat: But this means that the cross was not something done to him, but rather something done by Him.
delen.uitleg: A second speaker takes the other half: surrender with the things that are in our control. He reads John 10:17–18, where Jesus says no one takes His life from Him but He lays it down of His own accord: the cross was not something done to Him but something done by Him, and every day we face the same decision whether we will live a life of surrender. From Luke 4 he shows that Jesus was led by the Spirit into the desert and returned in the power of the Spirit; God spoke to Abraham, Moses, Isaiah and Jesus in the desert, so in a desert season you are closer to God than you think. What takes most leaders out is ego, everything that works against surrender. Public authority can only rest on private surrender, and you do not surrender by trying harder but by drawing nearer.
delen.vraag: Where does your own effort or ego get in the way, and what would drawing nearer to Jesus look like for you this week?

delen.titel: Not Your Reward but Your Gift
delen.citaat: The Holy Spirit is not the reward for your holiness. The Holy Spirit is the source of your holiness.
delen.uitleg: How do you surrender daily to someone you cannot see? With 1 Peter 1:8 and 2 Corinthians 5:7 the speaker answers: by faith, not by sight, and God did give the Spirit a body, yours. The Holy Spirit is the great revealer of Jesus; the more you surrender to Him, the closer you get to Jesus. The biggest thing that stops people is not feeling worthy, but He is not your reward, He is your gift: purity is not an accomplishment but a relationship, and the Spirit is the source of your holiness, not the reward for it. A young man came back after twelve months free from pornography after one touch of the Holy Spirit. We repent enough to be forgiven, but can we surrender enough to be changed? We get the Spirit at salvation, but the Spirit gets us at surrender.
delen.vraag: Where do you treat the Holy Spirit as a reward you have to earn, and how is it for you to receive Him as a gift that brings you closer to Jesus?

delen.titel: Empty Yourself, Yield to His Presence
delen.citaat: And the more you surrender to the anointed one, the more his anointing flows.
delen.uitleg: The Holy Spirit is not a power but a person: a power would surrender to you, a person you must surrender to, and He desires intimacy with you (James 4:5). In 1 Kings 19:11 Elijah does not find the Lord in the wind, the earthquake or the fire but in a still, small voice, and a voice can only belong to a person; relationship with the Spirit matters more than revelation from Him. The one thing the speaker wants to leave behind is to learn a life of surrender: empty yourself, yield to His presence, and learn to be a vessel of the Holy Spirit, a vessel of Jesus to this world. Then he leads the room: hands open, be still, ask the Holy Spirit to come, and surrender the hurt, the pain from the past and the bitterness. The Spirit does not come because of a song or a speaker but because Jesus promised He would.
delen.vraag: What are you still holding on to that you could surrender with open hands, trusting that He comes because Jesus promised?

luister.citaat: The Holy Spirit comes because Jesus promised you would.

uitnodiging.tekst: At the end the speaker teaches the room how to surrender: empty yourself, hands out with palms up, be still, and ask the Holy Spirit to come. He invites people to surrender the hurt, the pain from the past and the bitterness, and to receive what one moment with the Holy Spirit can bring.
uitnodiging.citaat: How you surrender is you empty yourself. You empty yourself. I like to put my hands out like this with my palms facing up. And I just ask the Holy Spirit to come.

gebedspunten.tekst: Thank You, God, that before we ever said 'here I am' to You, You said it to us, and that You showed it in Jesus, who laid His life down of His own accord.
Show us where we are making the outcome the condition of our obedience, and help us to say 'here I am' to You even in hardship, trusting the One we surrender to.
Holy Spirit, we ask You to come. We surrender the hurt, the pain from the past and the bitterness, and we want to be vessels of Jesus to the people around us.

And we say, would you come, Lord Jesus. And Jesus, you are the healer. Jesus, you told us to pray for healing. Jesus, you told us to expect greater things. And so we say for every person who is standing right now, body be healed in the name of Jesus. We say, body be healed in the name of Jesus. Lord, we pray for complete meaning and for every organ and every cell, every strand of DNA, every molecule, every neuron, Lord, we pray for complete restoration and complete healing of every body. Lord, we say bodies be healed in the name of Jesus. And Lord, we pray right now a transformed prognosis, a transformed diagnosis. Lord, we pray for confounded doctors, and we pray for astonished nurses. Lord, we pray for tears of joy. We pray for your presence with people. Lord, we pray that every person standing would know your presence with them in a way that they have never felt or understood before. Lord, we pray for testimony of people. We pray for testimonies of salvation. We pray for the restoration of families. We pray for your spirit to be at work in hospitals and in treatment centers. We say, Maranatha, would you come, Lord Jesus? In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

So Father God, we thank you that your presence is in this place and it's resting upon us. And you're moving through every chair, every aisle, and you're touching our hearts, and you're moving us into a surrendering reality.
